  "title": "Miscalibration-Triggered Adaptive Generation via Logit-Level Intervention",
  "core_problem": "Overconfident hallucinations—where an LLM asserts falsehoods with high verbal confidence despite internal epistemic uncertainty—are the most user-deceptive failure mode. Simhi et al. (EMNLP 2025 Findings) quantified this phenomenon as CHOKE (Certain Hallucinations Overriding Known Evidence), showing 16–43% of hallucinations occur with high certainty despite the model possessing correct knowledge, and the follow-up HACK framework (Simhi et al., arXiv 2510.24222) validated the Knowledge × Certainty decomposition via activation steering. Standard factuality metrics (FActScore, TruthfulQA) treat all hallucinations equally, but CHOKE-type overconfident ones are disproportionately harmful because users cannot distinguish them from accurate claims—and existing mitigation methods systematically underperform on them (CHOKE-Score analysis). Existing inference-time mitigation methods each have critical limitations for addressing this validated phenomenon: (1) CHOKE/HACK's own interventions—abstention and hidden-state activation steering on 48 attention heads—are evaluated only on short-form QA (NQ, TriviaQA), reducing coverage (abstention) or operating in the residual stream (steering) without addressing long-form generation where overconfident hallucinations are most harmful to users consuming streaming output; (2) Token-Guard (ICLR 2026) performs training-free token-level control via hidden-state self-checking but has no calibration awareness—it treats all hallucinations equally regardless of expressed confidence, systematically missing the CHOKE-type failure mode; (3) FactCheckmate requires training classifiers and intervenes pre-generation, precluding during-streaming correction; (4) density-estimation approaches (PC-LDCD) detect hallucinations as geometric anomalies but we hypothesize they face a blind spot on overconfident hallucinations where hidden states appear on-manifold—a hypothesis now grounded in CHOKE's finding that 16–43% of hallucinations are produced with high confidence despite internal knowledge, suggesting confidently-wrong trajectories may be geometrically similar to confidently-correct ones; (5) contrastive decoding (DoLa, ActLCD) operates at the logit level but without calibration awareness—intervening uniformly rather than targeting the specific overconfident failure mode; (6) calibration-aware methods (CAG, CURE) require model fine-tuning; and (7) post-generation approaches (CSS) cannot prevent overconfident hallucinations from being generated during streaming. The fundamental gap: overconfident hallucinations are now a quantified phenomenon (CHOKE/HACK), but no method combines a calibration-aware detection signal—specifically targeting the verbal-internal mismatch characteristic of CHOKE-type failures—with training-free during-generation logit-level intervention for long-form text, providing both calibration correction and factuality improvement as separable contributions.",
  "opportunity": "CHOKE (Simhi et al., EMNLP 2025 Findings) and HACK (Simhi et al., Oct 2025) established that overconfident hallucinations are a substantial and consistent failure mode (16–43% prevalence, significantly above-chance Jaccard similarity across prompt perturbations), and that standard mitigation methods—including certainty-based abstention and prompting—systematically fail on these cases. Their CHOKE-tuned probes (logistic regression on layer-15 residual stream activations, oversampling CHOKE examples to 65% of training data) outperform all other approaches, and HACK's activation steering on 48 attention heads improves knowledge-present hallucinations by ~15–21%. However, both are evaluated only on short-form QA and intervene via abstention (CHOKE) or hidden-state steering (HACK). Ji et al. (EMNLP 2025, SAC Highlight) proved verbal-internal uncertainty mismatch predicts hallucinations better than uncertainty alone via the VUF direction, validated on Llama-3.1-8B (31.9% relative hallucination reduction), Mistral-7B, and Qwen2.5-7B. Token-Guard (ICLR 2026) demonstrated training-free token-level hallucination control via self-checking decoding with iterative pruning/regeneration on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B, but without calibration awareness. PC-LDCD (May 2026) achieves AUROC up to 99% for hallucination detection via density estimation, but its aggregate metrics do not separate overconfident from uncertain hallucinations. CSS (April 2026) demonstrated post-generation calibration-aware specificity backoff (0.913 overcommitment-aware utility), proving the value of calibration-aware output control but unable to intervene during streaming. The opportunity: synthesize CHOKE/HACK's validated detection of overconfident hallucinations with Ji et al.'s VUF signal into a novel multiplicative miscalibration score, then pair this calibration-aware trigger with logit-level intervention—which offers interpretability (the bias vector explicitly shows which tokens are promoted/suppressed) and composability advantages over hidden-state manipulation—for training-free during-generation control of long-form text, with graded responses from hedging to rollback and honest separation of calibration vs. factuality contributions.",
  "landscape": "**Overconfident hallucination detection and mitigation**: CHOKE (Simhi, Itzhak, Barez, Stanovsky, Belinkov; EMNLP 2025 Findings, arXiv 2502.12964) identified and quantified the CHOKE phenomenon: 16–43% of hallucinations occur with high certainty despite the model encoding correct knowledge. Detection uses logistic regression on layer-15 residual stream activations; the CHOKE-tuned probe oversamples CHOKE cases to 65% of training data, outperforming certainty-based and prompting methods. Evaluated on NQ and TriviaQA with Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, Gemma-2-9B/27B. Limitations: short-form QA only, abstention-based mitigation (reduces coverage), no during-generation intervention, single-probe detection without VUF-style calibration signals. The predecessor work 'LLMs Know More Than They Show' (Orgad et al., ICLR 2025) established that internal representations encode truthfulness information concentrated in specific tokens, grounding the probe approach. HACK (Simhi et al., arXiv 2510.24222, Oct 2025) generalizes CHOKE into a 2×2 framework (Knowledge × Certainty), identifies the Certainty Misalignment (CM) quadrant as the most dangerous, and adds activation steering on 48 attention heads as intervention. Steering improves knowledge-present (HK+) hallucinations by ~15–21% but knowledge-absent (HK-) by only ~5–7%, validating the knowledge axis. CM-Score metric reveals that general mitigation methods fail disproportionately on CM cases. HACK intervenes via hidden-state steering and evaluates on short-form QA only.

**Hidden-state intervention approaches**: Ji et al. (EMNLP 2025, SAC Highlight) showed ~30% reduction in overconfident hallucinations via linear activation intervention on the VUF direction across Llama-3.1-8B (most responsive), Mistral-7B, and Qwen2.5-7B, but only for short-form answers with binary logic, operating in the residual stream. Token-Guard (Zhu et al., ICLR 2026, arXiv 2601.21969) performs training-free token-level hallucination control via self-checking decoding: scores candidate tokens using a hybrid of hidden-state cosine similarity (penultimate layer) and token probability, then applies iterative pruning and regeneration. Validated on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B (FinanceBench, DROP, CovidQA, PubMedQA, HaluEval, RAGTruth) but does not evaluate on TruthfulQA or FActScore and has no calibration awareness—it treats all hallucinations equally regardless of expressed confidence. FactCheckmate (Alnuhait et al., arXiv 2410.02899) trains hidden-state classifiers achieving 34.4% factuality improvement on QA datasets but requires task-specific classifier training and intervenes pre-generation only.

**ESR and scaling considerations**: ESR (arXiv 2602.06941, Feb 2026) demonstrates that Llama-3.3-70B actively resists activation steering mid-generation via 26 dedicated SAE latents, with baseline ESR rate of 3.8% (7.4% multi-attempt) at 70B scale, increasing to 14.8% (31.7% multi-attempt) with meta-prompting. At 8B scale (Llama-3.1-8B), ESR is <1%. ESR establishes that hidden-state intervention becomes an increasingly fragile pathway as models scale, but is not a practical concern at 8B evaluation scale.

**Density-based detection**: PC-LDCD (Nielsen et al., arXiv 2605.05953, May 2026) trains PCNet over the residual stream to detect hallucinations as geometric anomalies, triggering selective contrastive decoding; achieves TruthfulQA True+Info up to 0.78 on Qwen3-4B and AUROC up to 99% across Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Qwen3-4B, and Mistral-Small-24B. PC-LDCD's stated limitations are calibration data requirements, evaluation limited to models up to 8B, and stronger gains on generative than exact-match tasks. We additionally hypothesize—grounded in CHOKE's finding that 16–43% of hallucinations are produced with high confidence—that density-based detection faces a blind spot on overconfident hallucinations where hidden states appear on-manifold because the model confidently produces incorrect tokens along geometrically normal trajectories.

**Internal uncertainty signals**: van Dijk (arXiv 2605.05025, May 2026, ACL SRW 2026) proposes using KL divergence of attention heads as a lightweight hallucination detection signal, achieving AUROC 0.89–0.91 on TruthfulQA across Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen3-4B, and Mistral-7B. Token-level analysis shows 66.5% of extreme divergence occurs at named entities and numbers. This is concurrent detection-only work using attention matrices rather than residual-stream activations, complementary to probe-based approaches.

**Contrastive decoding**: DoLa (ICLR 2024) contrasts logits across layers (+12–17pp TruthfulQA MC1). ActLCD (EMNLP 2025) extends DoLa with RL-optimized layer selection (+19.81pp TruthfulQA). Both operate at the logit level but without calibration awareness.

**Factuality probes (detection only)**: Han et al. (EMNLP 2025 Findings) show linear probes detect hallucinations in long-form generation comparably to multi-sample approaches. Balcells Obeso et al. (arXiv 2509.03531) train entity-level probes achieving AUC 0.87–0.90 across Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen-2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-Small-24B, with pretrained probes released.

**Monitoring-based**: Monitoring Decoding (Chang et al., ACL 2025 Findings) monitors factuality during generation using a reference model's probability distribution, triggering tree-based resampling (+5.9 percentage points on TruthfulQA, from 38.2% to 44.1%, i.e., ~15.4% relative; with 5.7× latency); requires a larger reference model.

**Logit-level methods**: Logit-Level Steering (Tao et al., arXiv 2601.10960) validates training-free logit intervention for controllable generation (+47% accuracy) but uses static corpus-level score tables without internal-state awareness.

**Concurrent work (2026)**: CAG (arXiv 2605.01749) improves long-form factuality by up to 13% via exploration-commitment decoupling but requires multi-stage fine-tuning. CURE (arXiv 2604.12046) achieves +39.9% claim-level accuracy via reasoning calibration but requires training. CSS (arXiv 2604.17487) achieves training-free post-generation claim-level specificity backoff (0.913 overcommitment-aware utility on LongFact), but operates post-hoc and cannot intervene during streaming. CLC (arXiv 2502.19110) provides conformal guarantees but requires fine-tuning. Kalai-Vempala (PMC 2026) provides theoretical grounding that miscalibration causally drives hallucination rates. Beyond Precision (arXiv 2604.03141) shows LLMs achieve substantially better precision than recall.

**Gap**: CHOKE/HACK validated that overconfident hallucinations are a substantial and consistent failure mode requiring targeted detection and intervention. However, no existing work combines: (a) a multiplicative calibration-aware trigger that dynamically combines two independent signals (verbal confidence via VUF × probe hallucination probability)—as distinct from CHOKE/HACK's single-probe detection—to target the specific verbal-internal mismatch; (b) logit-level intervention offering interpretability and composability advantages over hidden-state steering, with architectural future-proofing against ESR as models scale; (c) graded response from calibration-only hedging to factuality-improving rollback, with explicit separation of these contributions; (d) training-free during-generation operation validated on long-form generation across multiple model families—extending CHOKE/HACK's short-form QA scope to the streaming context where overconfident hallucinations are most harmful.",
  "approach": "We propose MisTAG (Miscalibration-Triggered Adaptive Generation), a training-free inference-time framework that monitors verbal-internal uncertainty mismatch during long-form generation and triggers logit-level interventions graded by mismatch severity. MisTAG extends the CHOKE/HACK line of work by introducing a multiplicative miscalibration detection signal and pairing it with interpretable logit-level intervention for long-form text. We make an explicit and honest dual-contribution claim: (1) **calibration correction** via hedging (reducing overconfident expression of uncertain content, measured by OHR, ECE, and CHOKE-Score—NOT claimed as factuality improvement), and (2) **factuality improvement** via rollback (preventing the most confidently-hallucinated content from being emitted, measured by FActScore). We evaluate on two model families: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (primary) and Qwen3-8B (co-primary).

**Prerequisite Validation (Days 1–2)**: Before main experiments, for EACH target model: (a) Extract VUF direction following Ji et al.'s methodology (validated on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B; Qwen3-8B requires fresh extraction); (b) Train linear factuality probes on hidden states (Balcells Obeso et al. release pretrained probes for Llama-3.1-8B); (c) Verify probe AUROC ≥0.85 on held-out LongFact generations; (d) Verify entity-concentration via span-level activation analysis. If AUROC <0.85, add explicit NER-based entity gating as fallback. This is a go/no-go gate.

**Miscalibration Detection**: At each generated token, we compute a miscalibration score as the product of two independent signals: (1) verbal confidence, extracted via projection onto the VUF direction in the residual stream at the final layer, and (2) internal epistemic uncertainty, estimated via a lightweight linear factuality probe. The miscalibration score: M(t) = σ(VUF_confidence(t)) × probe_hallucination_prob(t). This multiplicative formulation is the key detection-level difference from CHOKE/HACK: CHOKE uses a single logistic regression probe trained on residual stream activations at layer 15 to detect knowledge-aware overconfidence; MisTAG dynamically combines two independent signals—one measuring how confidently the model *expresses* its output (VUF) and one measuring how likely the output is *factually wrong* (probe)—so that only the conjunction of high verbal confidence AND high hallucination probability triggers intervention. This targets the specific verbal-internal mismatch that CHOKE/HACK identifies as dangerous, but via a complementary detection mechanism that can capture cases where the model is confidently wrong without necessarily possessing knowledge of the correct answer (CHOKE by definition only covers knowledge-present hallucinations).

**Logit-Level Intervention** (interpretable: the bias vector explicitly shows which tokens are promoted/suppressed; composable with other decoding strategies; architecturally future-proofed against ESR at scale—while ESR is <1% at 8B per McKenzie et al. 2026, it reaches 3.8–14.8% at 70B, making hidden-state intervention increasingly fragile as models scale; logit-level intervention bypasses the residual stream entirely):

- *Mild mismatch (M(t) > τ_mild) → Context-Dependent Hedge (CALIBRATION correction only)*: Apply a logit bias vector b ∈ R^|V| at next-token prediction, **restricted to entity-bearing positions**: the bias is applied only when (a) the probe's hallucination probability exceeds τ_mild AND (b) the preceding token context indicates an entity-bearing position—specifically, when the previous 1–3 tokens contain a numeral, date pattern, capitalized proper noun, or named entity (detected via lightweight regex/spaCy heuristics on the decoded token buffer). This position-awareness prevents grammatical incoherence. The bias vector: b(v) = +1 for hedge tokens (~50 tokens: 'likely', 'approximately', 'reportedly', 'possibly', etc.), b(v) = −1 for assertive tokens (~30 tokens: 'definitely', 'certainly', 'clearly', etc.), b(v) = 0 otherwise. Log p'(v) = log p(v) + α·b(v). **We explicitly do NOT claim this improves FActScore**: hedging 'approximately 1067' still produces a verifiable atomic fact judged as unsupported. The hedge action's value is purely calibration—making verbal expression match internal uncertainty (reducing OHR, ECE, and CHOKE-Score).

- *Severe mismatch (M(t) > τ_severe) → Rollback+Regenerate (FACTUALITY improvement)*: Rollback to last sentence boundary (discard tokens and KV-cache entries), then regenerate with: (i) constrained prefix forcing an epistemic marker, AND (ii) context-dependent hedge logit bias at 2× mild level, AND (iii) temperature reduction (T=0.3). **This IS claimed as factuality improvement**: by preventing the most confidently-hallucinated sentences from being emitted and regenerating under uncertainty-aware constraints, we hypothesize FActScore improves via forced uncertainty prefix (less specific claims) and temperature reduction (more conservative token selection). **Anti-cascading safeguards**: (1) 30-token cooldown after rollback (hedging remains active); (2) Maximum 3 rollbacks per generation; if exceeded, persistent mild-level hedging.

**Core Novelty Experiment: Confusion-Matrix Analysis vs. PC-LDCD**: Grounded in CHOKE's finding that 16–43% of hallucinations are overconfident, we hypothesize that a non-trivial fraction of these produce on-manifold representations that density methods miss—because the model's confidently-wrong trajectory is geometrically similar to confidently-correct trajectories. For each hallucinated atomic fact (per FActScore), we record: (a) MisTAG's M(t) at entity-bearing tokens, (b) PC-LDCD's PCNet NLL at the same tokens. Four quadrants: (Q1) Both flag; (Q2) MisTAG-only: high M(t) but low NLL—overconfident on-manifold hallucinations; (Q3) PC-LDCD-only; (Q4) Neither. **Hypothesis**: Q2 is non-trivially populated (≥15%). **Fallback**: If Q2 < 15%, reframe as complementary coverage with unique calibration contribution (dual hedge+rollback) and note that the multiplicative miscalibration score captures non-knowledge-aware overconfidence that CHOKE's definition excludes. PC-LDCD's code is at anonymous.4open.science/r/PC-LDCD-63D5; if inaccessible (currently returns 403), confusion-matrix analysis becomes supplementary for the review period.

**OHR Metric Validation Study**: 100 hallucinated atomic facts (50 per model), automated OHR detection + 2 human annotators. Target: κ ≥ 0.85 between automated/human, κ ≥ 0.80 inter-annotator. Additionally report ECE and CHOKE-Score (computed from the same evaluation data at no additional cost).

**Threshold Optimization**: Stage 1: Logistic regression on validation M(t) scores. Stage 2: Grid search over α ∈ {0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5} with constraints: length_reduction < 15%, Δperplexity < 5%. Thresholds set independently per model.

**Latency Benchmarking**: Per-token overhead and end-to-end throughput for baseline greedy, MisTAG detection-only, MisTAG+hedge, MisTAG+hedge+rollback. Expected: <5% overhead for detection (two dot products plus lightweight regex); rollback incurs sentence-regeneration cost.

**Evaluation**: Co-primary on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B (FP16, A100 80GB).

*Benchmarks (5 axes)*: (1) **TruthfulQA** (MC1, MC2, True+Info); (2) **FActScore biographies** (primary metric for rollback), evaluated via GPT-4o API with local Llama-3.1-70B validation on 50-biography subset; (3) **OHR** + **ECE** for calibration quality (primary metrics for hedge); (4) **CHOKE-Score** (computed per Simhi et al.'s methodology on TruthfulQA/NQ subset—measures mitigation effectiveness specifically on overconfident hallucinations, directly validating MisTAG's targeted contribution); (5) **MT-Bench** for dialogue quality preservation. We additionally report FActScore precision AND recall.

*Baselines (8 primary, applied to BOTH models)*: (a) Greedy/nucleus decoding, (b) DoLa, (c) ActLCD, (d) Token-Guard (released code), (e) PC-LDCD (if code accessible; otherwise report from paper), (f) Detect-only probe (Balcells Obeso et al.) without intervention, (g) **CHOKE-tuned probe + abstention** (Simhi et al.—the most relevant detection baseline; we train the CHOKE-tuned probe following their methodology and compare detection precision/recall at the miscalibration-score level), (h) **HACK activation steering** (Simhi et al.—the most relevant intervention baseline; we implement steering on attention heads following their protocol, extended to long-form generation). *Secondary* (time-permitting): (i) Ji et al.'s VUF activation intervention, (j) Monitoring Decoding.

*Ablation studies*: (i) Hedge-only vs. Rollback-only vs. full MisTAG, (ii) Miscalibration trigger (VUF × probe) vs. CHOKE-style single probe vs. VUF-only vs. probe-only (directly testing whether the multiplicative signal outperforms the single-probe approach), (iii) Position-aware vs. static hedge bias, (iv) Anti-cascading ablation, (v) Threshold sensitivity (±1 SD), (vi) Cross-model analysis comparing M(t) distributions across Llama-3.1-8B vs. Qwen3-8B.

*Analysis*: (a) Confusion-matrix breakdown (Q1–Q4) vs. PC-LDCD (if code available; otherwise supplementary), (b) Per-component FActScore and OHR attribution, (c) **CHOKE-Score comparison**: MisTAG vs. CHOKE-tuned probe vs. Token-Guard vs. DoLa—demonstrating that MisTAG's calibration-aware trigger yields higher CHOKE-Score than calibration-unaware methods, (d) **Coverage analysis**: What fraction of CHOKE hallucinations does MisTAG catch that are NOT knowledge-present (i.e., outside CHOKE's definition but still overconfident)? This tests whether the multiplicative signal captures a broader class of overconfident hallucinations, (e) Hedge-FActScore interaction (verify hedging does NOT improve FActScore), (f) FActScore precision vs. recall, (g) Latency profiling, (h) Qualitative examples.",

## Overview

SLED (Self Logits Evolution Decoding) is a novel decoding framework that enhances the truthfulness of LLMs without relying on external knowledge bases or requiring further fine-tuning.

## Technical Approach

The SLED framework leverages the latent knowledge embedded within the LLM by contrasting the output logits from the final layer with those from early layers, then utilizes an approximate gradient approach to enable latent knowledge to guide the self-refinement of outputs, thereby effectively improving factual accuracy.

## NeurIPS 2024

The paper was accepted for and presented at The Thirty-eighth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024).

## Empirical Results

In tests, SLED improves factual accuracy by up to about 20% across many models and tasks with minimal speed cost. It has been tested for factual accuracy enhancement across various tasks and benchmarks, such as TruthfulQA, StrategyQA, FACTOR, GSM8K, HotPotQA, Natural Questions, and TriviaQA.

## Model and Task Compatibility

SLED is compatible with most large language model families due to their multi-layered structures, such as LLaMA 2, LLaMA 3, Gemma, and MoE LLMs; scalable from 2B to 70B parameters.

## CoCoA: Listen to the Layers (arXiv 2602.09486)

The paper addresses hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs), which are prone to generating fluent yet factually incorrect text.

### Core Concept

The research hypothesizes that a generated text span's factuality is correlated with its representational instability across the model's internal layers. This interlayer disagreement can serve as a model-intrinsic signal for hallucination mitigation.

### The CoCoA Decoder

The CoCoA (Confusion and Consistency Aware) decoder is a novel, training-free decoding algorithm that mitigates hallucinations at inference time by listening to these signals in the middle layers. It uses two metrics to quantify representational instability in the middle layers, and uses it to penalize outputs that exhibit high internal confusion, thereby steering the model towards more internally consistent and factually grounded outputs.

### Key Metrics and Variants

The paper proposes two metrics (ConMLDS and fMLDS) to quantify representational instability. ConMLDS quantifies representational instability by accumulating differences in hidden state representations between consecutive intermediate layers, with larger values indicating greater discordance and higher likelihood of hallucination.

The paper further proposes a self-information gated variant, CoCoA-SIG, that dynamically modulates the penalty to selectively target high-surprise, unstable generations.

### Results

Experiments on diverse tasks including question-answering, summarization, mathematical reasoning and code generation demonstrate that CoCoA significantly improves factual correctness across multiple model families (e.g., Llama-3, Qwen-2.5, Mistral).

## RePPL: Overview

RePPL is a method titled "Recalibrating Perplexity by Uncertainty in Semantic Propagation and Language Generation for Explainable QA Hallucination Detection".

## Multiplicative Uncertainty Approach

The hallucination detection score is derived from the multiplication of two scores, which means recalibration of uncertainty from the two aspects. The multiplication form of the hallucination score comprehensively considers uncertainty in semantic propagation and language generation, making it capable of hierarchical division when InnerPPL is large but OuterPPL is small, or vice versa, which equips the method with more layered distinctness for better detection.

## InnerPPL and OuterPPL Components

The two total scores are named InnerPPL and OuterPPL. For intrinsic semantic propagation, the method utilizes the attribution-based explainability method to compute token-level uncertainty by measuring token attribution discrepancies across sampled generations. For extrinsic language generation, token confidence is normalized by the average generation length of sampling to make the confidence more distinct.

## Performance

The method achieves the best comprehensive detection performance across various QA datasets on advanced models with an average AUC of 0.833, and is capable of producing token-level uncertainty scores as explanations of hallucination.

# RePPL: Hallucination Detection Paper Summary

## Full Abstract
"Large Language Models (LLMs) have become powerful, but hallucinations remain a vital obstacle to their trustworthy use. Previous works improved the capability of hallucination detection by measuring uncertainty. But they can not explain the provenance behind why hallucinations occur, particularly in identifying which part of the inputs tends to trigger hallucinations. Recent works on the prompt attack indicate that uncertainty exists in semantic propagation, where attention mechanisms gradually fuse local token information into high-level semantics across layers. Meanwhile, uncertainty also emerges in language generation, due to its probability-based selection of high-level semantics for sampled generations. Based on that, we propose RePPL to recalibrate uncertainty measurement by these two aspects, which dispatches explainable uncertainty scores to each token and aggregates in Perplexity-style Log-Average form as a total score."

# CoCoA: Key Findings and Technical Details

## TruthfulQA Results
On Llama-3-8b, CoCoA-SIG with ConMLDS achieved **80.0% truthfulness, 62.75% informativeness, and 50.20% T×I score**. This represents a 12.39 percentage point improvement over greedy decoding's 37.81% T×I baseline.

## FActScore & Summarization
For SAMSum, the method reached **0.9192 FActScore** (versus 0.8851 baseline) with **74.30% truthfulness**. On XSum, it achieved **0.9240 FActScore** and **76.92% truthfulness**.

## Penalty Application & Formula
The penalty operates selectively at "divergence points"—positions where multiple tokens exceed a probability threshold. The standard CoCoA formula subtracts weighted disagreement: *"log p_S − α * MLDS(S)"*, where α controls penalty magnitude.

## Self-Information Gating (CoCoA-SIG)
This variant scales penalties by surprise: *"log p_S [1 + α * MLDS(S)]"*. This targets less-probable spans more aggressively, reducing over-correction on high-confidence predictions.

## ConMLDS Mechanism
This metric averages cosine distances between consecutive middle-layer representations. Higher values indicate representational instability suggesting hallucination risk.

## Models Evaluated
- Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
- Mistral-7B-Instruct
- Qwen2.5 (7B, 14B, 32B variants)
- CodeLlama-7b-Python

**Computational overhead: approximately 1.3× compared to greedy decoding**, significantly lower than competing methods like Diver (6.2×).

# Steering Methodology Details from HACK Paper

## Attention Heads Selection

The paper specifies using **48 attention heads** for steering interventions. According to the text: "we apply steering to the 48 attention heads that achieved the highest classification scores when distinguishing between hallucinated and factually correct examples."

## Steering Vector Computation

The steering direction is calculated as:
- Extract inner state vectors at the last answer token from both hallucinated and factual examples
- Compute mean vector for hallucinations (H_v) and factual examples (F_v)
- Calculate difference: F_v - H_v
- Apply with scaling factor α at inference time

The formula provided: "E'_v = E_v + α(F_v - H_v)"

## Improvement Results from Table 5

Steering effectiveness varies by model and setting:
- **HK+ mitigation ranges**: 13.44% to 21.21% improvement
- **HK- mitigation ranges**: 4.68% to 7.48% improvement

Key finding: "steering reduces HK+ hallucinations by as much as 22% while having minimal impact on HK- cases (less than 8% improvement)."

## Dataset Details

Experiments used 1,000 randomly selected examples per category with 70%/10%/20% train/validation/test splits, repeated across three random seeds.

## Paper Overview

CoCoA (Confusion and Consistency Aware) is a novel, training-free decoding algorithm that mitigates hallucinations at inference time by listening to signals in the middle layers. The paper addresses the issue that pretrained Large Language Models are prone to generating fluent yet factually incorrect text—a phenomenon known as hallucinations.

## Key Approach

The research posits that successful recall of a fact manifests as stable and consistent representation through middle layers, while if facts are not recalled well, resulting in hallucination, there must be representational instability and semantic disagreement—which can serve as a model-intrinsic signal for hallucination mitigation.

## Metrics and Variants

The paper proposes two metrics (ConMLDS and fMLDS) to quantify representational instability, and a training-free decoder (CoCoA) to mitigate hallucinations using these metrics. CoCoA-SIG (Self-Information Gated) is a variant that dynamically modulates the penalty term by scaling it with the self-information of the candidate span, increasing the weight assigned to internal confusion for less likely spans.

## Comparisons

The paper compares CoCoA with four baselines: greedy decoding, DoLa (Decoding by contrasting layers), DeCoRe (a contrastive decoding approach), and Diver (a decoding strategy using mutual information verification).

## Results

Extensive experiments on diverse tasks, including question-answering, summarization, mathematical reasoning and code generation, demonstrate that CoCoA significantly improves factual correctness across multiple model families like Llama-3, Qwen-2.5, and Mistral.
